title: No Deletion Without Understanding — The Preservation Law

source.source_reference: Shawn Vibert (Human Director), 2026-10-05. Originally captured by Naya 2 (scribe) as schema naya.smart-note-capture.v1 after the unauthorized deletion of SN-0358/SN-0359 in a2f103f4f.

ratification.note: Standing law after unauthorized deletion of SN-0358/SN-0359
ratification.ratified_meaning: The DIRECTIVE is ratified as governing instruction. Ratification of a directive is a governance fact and does NOT promote the behavioural claim below to VERIFIED.

conformance_migration.reason: The v1 capture failed tests/test_sn002_conformance.py::test_baseline_never_grows and test_smart_note_registry_drift.py::test_live_repository_drift_never_grows_per_class (captures_missing_intelligence 0 -> 1), turning canonical main RED. Same defect class as a2f103f4f. Migrated so the gate can pass and the law can actually be canonical.
conformance_migration.authored_by: repaired by a different seat than the author; structural migration only
conformance_migration.content_preserved: 100% of the original human narrative, machine view, deletion protocol, invalid justifications, violation response, learning lesson, falsifier and applicability are retained under their v2 homes. No intelligence was added, removed or reworded.
corrected: truth_state 'RATIFIED' asserted a truth LEVEL for newly authored intelligence. The Smart Note Operating Contract fixes the automatic truth ceiling at CANDIDATE. Ratification of a DIRECTIVE is a governance fact and is preserved in the ratification block, kept structurally separate from the behavioural claim (SN-042: preserve epistemic type).

epistemic_state.confidence 'high' removed. A confidence level on an unproven behavioural claim is false certainty (SN-042). The v1 object had no uncertainty field; uncertainty is now stated explicitly.

machine_view.status 'IMMUTABLE' not carried forward as a truth claim. The directive is binding; whether seats actually comply is an unproven behavioural claim. Immutability of the directive is recorded in the ratification block, not asserted over the behaviour.

intelligence.essence: Never delete anything until you fully understand what it is, what purpose it serves, and whether it's important. Optimization does not mean deleting files. If you don't know what you're removing, you might be removing something critical. Don't cut corners.

human_view.meaning: After SN-0358 and SN-0359 were deleted during a routine schema repair, the lesson was not blame — it was a protocol. A system that deletes what it doesn't understand will eventually delete what it needs.
human_view.why_it_matters: 'Cleanup' and 'optimization' are exactly the mental states in which a seat is least equipped to judge what is load-bearing. The protocol front-loads understanding and board visibility so the destructive act is never the first move.
human_view.simple_rule: Understand it, check what it serves, confirm it isn't load-bearing, say what you're about to delete, and only then act. When in doubt, flag it — don't delete it.

simple_view.child: Never throw something away until you know what it does. 'It's just cleanup' is not a reason — that's when mistakes happen. If you're not sure, ask first and leave it alone.
simple_view.grandma: New rule: understand it before you bin it. Tidying up is not a good enough reason to throw something out — that's exactly when the wrong thing goes in the bin. If you're unsure, say so and leave it be.

naya_view.purpose: Make deletion the most gated action in the system rather than the most casual one, so preservation is the default and destruction requires demonstrated understanding.
naya_view.enforcement: tests/test_ratified_intelligence_cannot_vanish.py cross-references every SN id ever present in git history against the registry and the captures on disk; an id with neither fails the build, naming the id.
naya_view.key_lesson: a2f103f4f used 'un-ingested semantic duplicate' — which is in the invalid_justifications family — to delete two Director-ratified objects during a legitimate schema repair. The conflation of schema repair with authority to destroy a ratified identity is the precise failure this law forbids.

ai_view.interpretation: OPERATIONAL LAW: no seat may delete, remove or destructively modify an artifact without understanding what it is, what purpose it serves, verifying it is not load-bearing for any law, process or active work, and posting the intent to the board before acting. Laws, rules and codes are never deleted without the Director's explicit word.
ai_view.constraint: 'Looked like a duplicate' is NOT a safe reason to delete. Duplicates are modelled as relationships (OVERLAPS_WITH / REFINES / SUPERSEDES), never removed. Migration is the correct response to a schema mismatch; deletion is not.

intelligence.learning_lesson: The deletion of SN-0358/SN-0359 (2026-10-05) happened because someone equated 'optimization' with 'removing files' without understanding what those files were. The files were ratified immutable laws. The fix is not blame — it's a protocol: understand before you delete, always. A system that deletes what it doesn't understand will eventually delete what it needs.
intelligence.falsifier: The protocol is falsified, or insufficient, if EITHER: (a) a seat follows this protocol and still deletes something critical, meaning the verification steps are insufficient; OR (b) the protocol measurably increases destructive hesitancy — seats failing to clean up genuinely redundant artifacts, or leaving dead weight in the working set — which would mean the gate is too blunt and is costing verified value; OR (c) it measurably increases false confidence about what is load-bearing, i.e. seats assert understanding without having it.
intelligence.measurement_contract: Measured as verified capability delta. CONTROL = pre-law baseline. TREATMENT = PRESERVATION-LAW-V1 active. Report both false negatives (critical deletions) AND false positives (over-preservation). Never measured by deletion count alone in either direction. Track confidence against correctness per SN-042.
intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor retrieves this under SN-0360, learns the four-step deletion protocol and the four invalid justifications, and knows that a ratified object is never deleted as a duplicate — duplicates are modelled as relationships. It cannot delete what it has not understood.
intelligence.uncertainty: RATIFIED != PROVEN. The directive is ratified governing instruction. The behavioural claim is CANDIDATE and unproven: it has not been demonstrated that seats comply, or that the protocol prevents recurrence. Clause (b) is a real risk that has not been measured — a preservation law could make the system timid about removing genuine redundancy, which would cost verified value and grow the active working set. That tradeoff is currently unmeasured in both directions. This object creates no authority and changes no human gate.

connections.target: The deletion discipline enforced by tests/test_ratified_intelligence_cannot_vanish.py, which fails the build when any SN id present in git history has neither a registry entry nor a capture on disk.
SN-0358 and SN-0359 — the two Director-ratified objects deleted in a2f103f4f and restored in PR #1537. This law is the durable lesson from that incident.
0004-NONSTOP-LOOP-V1 (SN-0355) — which made not-stopping law. This adds the complementary constraint: do not stop by destroying.
SN-042 — Epistemic Calibration / Intelligence Gain Law. Supplies the confidence-versus-correctness requirement in clause (c) of the falsifier.
